basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'Vers. 7. Filii Chus Saba. Id est, Arabia regio thurifera. Hevila pars Aethiopiae'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 7. Filii Chus Saba. Id est, Arabia regio thurifera. Hevila pars Aethiopiae Occidentalis. Sabatha, Regma et Sabatacha. Horum nomina ab usu recesserunt, et quae pro eis nunc habeantur ignoramus. Filii Regma Saba. Alia est haec Saba quam illa quae superius legitur, et differt in Scriptura. Nam illa per Sin, haec per Samech scribitur. Nam et in psalmo ubi nos canimus: Reges Arabum et Saba (Psal. LXXI, 10), in Hebraeo habetur: Reges Saba et Saba. Dadan | Aethiopiae ultima regio est.
